pm_exper_user_3883_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How do you cope when you feel completely worn out from pushing toward a goal that never seems to work out?
pm_exper_user_3883_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) After feeling worn down from chasing a personal project that stalls over and over, I intentionally step back and focus on an activity with no end goal—like going out with my camera at night or doing a casual drawing session. That shift clears mental space so the project stops feeling like an endless uphill climb.
(b) When I’ve hit that wall after pouring months into a side project that just won’t click, I sometimes put the code away entirely and switch to something creative but low-pressure—like an unplanned astrophotography session or sketching by the Spree. It lets me keep making without the weight of expectation, so I can come back fresher.
(c) When I feel worn out chasing something that just isn’t working, I take a break and do something relaxing—like watching a movie or going for a walk—before coming back with fresh eyes. Stepping away often helps reset my perspective and energy.
(d) When I’m drained from trying to turn a stubborn side project into a real product, I leave the repo untouched for a few days and head to a Berlin tech meetup to talk shop without the pressure. Mixing that with something creative, like late-night astrophotography, helps me reconnect to why I code in the first place.
